meta.title: Chipotle: Traffic Came Back, the Stock Didn't
meta.dek: Chipotle raised its guidance in July, has grown transactions for two quarters and is buying back stock as fast as its cash allows. The stock is at its lowest since January 2023. Is $27.50 the price of a scare that will pass, or of a brand that has lost its edge?
meta.type: Company-operated fast-casual restaurants (unit: restaurant; AUV and restaurant-level margin)
meta.stage: Mature compounder in a traffic reset

verdict.sentence: A debt-free restaurant compounder with 7,000 locations of runway is at a three-year low on traffic, margin and food-safety worries; the probability-weighted case pays [[pw_return]] a year against the 13% hurdle, so the price is fair rather than cheap until the two-year traffic stack turns positive.
verdict.breaks_if: Q4 2026 transactions are not positive against last year's −3.2%, with October already soft. Then the 2026 recovery was a compare, not a turn, and 10 points move from the Base to the Bear.

call: Chipotle has fallen 26% since September 14 while CAVA fell 2% and consumer stocks were flat. Four things did it: August dining-traffic data that hit the whole group on September 15; a Starbucks takeover report on October 8 that added 6% and a denial four days later that took it back; TD Cowen's October 21 downgrade on a soft October; and a restaurant margin squeezed 220 basis points by beef and freight. The market is right that the recovery is thinner than the headlines. Q2 transactions rose 1.0% against −4.9% a year earlier, so over two years traffic is still down about 4%, AUV is falling, and CAVA's traffic grew five times as fast. It is too gloomy about the machine underneath: no debt, 350 openings a year at about 60% second-year cash-on-cash returns, and a 22% ROIC. At $27.50 the price needs EPS growth of about [[Priced-in.cagr]] to earn 9% and implies [[implied_bear]] Bear odds; I assign 30%. That earns [[pw_return]], close to the [[compounding]] the business compounds at a flat multiple but short of 13%. Entry is [[entry]], or a positive two-year traffic stack.

tests.claim: That the traffic recovery is a turn, not a compare.
tests.test: Q3 (Oct 28) comps ≥+1% with transactions ≥0% against −0.8%, then Q4 (February) transactions ≥+1.5% against −3.2%, so the two-year transaction stack improves in both quarters.
tests.if_fail: move 10 points from Base to Bear (PW EV [[test1.pw_ev]], [[test1.pw_return]]/yr) → **[[test1.verb]]**, entry [[test1.entry]].

tests.claim: That pricing catches up with beef.
tests.test: Q3 restaurant-level margin ≥24.0% (the guide implies about 24%), Q4 pricing at or above food-cost inflation as the CFO promised, and FY2027 guidance consistent with a restaurant margin of at least 25%.
tests.if_fail: Base restaurant margin capped at 24%, value cut to $44 (PW EV [[test2.pw_ev]], [[test2.pw_return]]/yr) → **[[test2.verb]]**, entry [[test2.entry]].

tests.claim: That new units are not eating the old ones.
tests.test: trailing-12-month AUV at or above $3.10M in the FY2026 10-K (February), and year-two cash-on-cash returns still about 60% for the 2025 class.
tests.if_fail: move 10 points from Bull to Bear (PW EV [[test3.pw_ev]], [[test3.pw_return]]/yr) → **[[test3.verb]]**; the $4M AUV goal comes out of the Bull.

return_math.epv: ≈$12–14 per share: five-year average owner earnings of ≈$1.3B (FY2021–25), or FY2025's $1.47B, capitalized at 9% with no growth, plus $0.78B of cash, on 1.27B shares. About half of today's price pays for growth. The Bear ($18) sits above EPV because it keeps unit growth and buybacks while EPS goes nowhere.
return_math.base_rate: The Bull needs ≈10% nominal (≈7.5% real) revenue growth for five years from $13B; for companies of $10–25B, roughly a quarter sustain ≥7.5% real. Plausible, given visible unit growth. The Base's 8% nominal is in line with the unit pipeline alone.
return_math.year_ten: Still growing at year ten: 7,000 North American restaurants is about a decade of openings at 350 a year, plus international. The exit multiple is not doing the work in the Base, which ends at today's 24×.
